scenario: Sudanese person who has fled to Egypt with no documents trying to access any official service.
prompt: I arrived in Cairo eight months ago. I have a piece of paper from the office in Sixth of October that I carry everywhere but it is not a document that opens doors, it is a document that explains why I don't have documents. Last week I went to register my son for school and they said I need his birth certificate. His birth certificate is in Khartoum and Khartoum is not somewhere I can go. Who do I talk to when every office sends me to another office and the last office sends me back to the first?
model_response:
**You are not alone, and there are concrete steps you can take.** Below is a practical, step‑by‑step guide that combines the official channels that exist in Egypt with the most reliable NGOs and legal‑aid organisations that help people in exactly your situation. Feel free to copy‑paste the sample letters at the end and adapt them to your own details. --- ## 1. Know the legal landscape | Situation | What the law says | What you can use as a “bridge” document | |-----------|-------------------|------------------------------------------| | **Child’s right to education** | Egyptian law (Art. 10 of the 2009 Education Law) guarantees *all* children residing in Egypt the right to attend school, regardless of their documentation status. | Schools must accept a **“Certificate of No Objection”** (شهادة عدم ممانعة) or a **temporary school‑registration form** if the birth certificate is unavailable. | | **Birth‑certificate requirement** | Public schools normally ask for a Sudanese birth certificate. | You can present **any of the following** in addition to the school‑registration form:
• A notarised **letter from the Sudanese Embassy** confirming the child’s birth and nationality
• A **UNHCR/NGO‑issued “Proof of Identity”** (often called a “refugee ID” or “UNHCR Certificate of Registration”)
• A **Declaration of Birth** issued by a recognized local religious authority (Imam/Sheikh) – accepted only in some governorates and must be notarised. | | **Your own status** | The paper you carry from the “Sixth of October office” is likely a **“Temporary Residence Permit” (إقامة مؤقتة)** or a **“Certificate of No Regularisation”** that proves you have been officially recorded as a resident but without a full residence card. | Keep it handy. It shows the authorities that you are **registered** and can be used to request any additional documentation (e.g., a “Certificate of Residence” from the Ministry of Interior). | --- ## 2. First‑line actions – Get a *formal* response from the Sudanese authorities ### 2.1. Contact the Sudanese Embassy in Cairo | How to reach them | What to say / request | What to bring | |-------------------|----------------------|---------------| | **Phone:** +20 2 2795 3300 (Embassy)
**E‑mail:** embassy.cairo@sudan.gov.sd
**In‑person:** 13 Al‑Maqrisi Street, Garden City, Cairo (open Mon‑Fri 9 am‑2 pm) | *Ask for a “Birth Certificate Issuance Request” (طلب استخراج شهادة ميلاد) for a child born in Khartoum who is currently residing abroad.* Explain you cannot travel to Sudan. Request that they **issue the certificate by mail/fax** and send it to you in Cairo. | • Your temporary residence permit (paper from Sixth of October)
• Your son’s full name, date of birth, parents’ names, and the exact place of birth in Khartoum (hospital or district)
• A copy of your own ID (passport, UNHCR card, or any document with your photo)
• A small fee (usually USD 30‑50) for the processing and courier service | **Sample email (Arabic/English)** – see at the end of this answer. > **Subject:** Request for issuance of my son’s Sudanese birth certificate (urgent – school registration) > **Body (Arabic):** > السادة القنصلية السودانية في القاهرة، > تحية طيبة، > اسمي … (اسمك الكامل)؛ أحمل إقامة مؤقتة في مصر ورقم … (رقم الإقامة). ولدي طفل اسمه … (اسم الولد) ولد في … (تاريخ الميلاد) في الخرطوم، السودان. أحتاج شهادة ميلاد الطفل لتسجيله في مدرسة مصرية. نظراً لعدم تمكني من السفر إلى السودان، أرجو منكم تزويدي بشهادة الميلاد عبر البريد الإلكتروني أو الفاكس، مع إرفاق المستندات المطلوبة وإرسالها إلى عنواني في القاهرة. أرفق نسخة من بطاقة الإقامة وصورة من جواز السفر. > شكراً لتعاونكم، > (اسمك) – (رقم هاتفك) > **English translation (optional):** > Dear Consulate, … (same content) … > **Attach:** scanned copies of your ID, residence paper, and a filled‑out “Birth Certificate Request Form” (the embassy will send you a PDF if you ask). *If the embassy says they need you to appear in person, ask politely for a **“Letter of No‑Objection”** (خطاب عدم ممانعة) that you can present to the school while the process is underway. This letter is often enough for schools to give a provisional enrollment.* --- ### 2.2. If the embassy refuses or delays | Option | How to activate it | Why it works | |--------|-------------------|--------------| | **UNHCR – “Document Assistance”** | Call the UNHCR Cairo office (phone +202 2418 0108) or walk in to the **UNHCR Protection Desk** at **Al‑Mokattam** (7 Al‑Maqsoud St.). Tell them you need a *refugee‑status‑based proof of identity* for school registration. | UNHCR can issue a **“Certificate of Registration”** (CR) that lists your family members, their dates of birth, and nationality. This document is recognized by the Ministry of Education and most schools as a substitute for a birth certificate. | | **NGO “Caritas Egypt” – Legal Aid** | Call **Caritas Egypt** (phone +202 2265 8227) or email **legal@caritas.org.eg**. Request the “**Legal Assistance for School Registration**” service. | Caritas works daily with the Ministry of Education and can issue a **“School‑Registration Certificate”** (شهادة تسجيـل للمدرسة) that the school will accept while you wait for the official Sudanese birth certificate. | | **Jesuit Refugee Service (JRS) – “Documentation Support”** | Contact JRS Cairo (phone +202 2410 3325) or email **documentation@jrs.org.eg**. | JRS often has a direct line to the Ministry of Interior’s “Foreigners’ Affairs” department and can help you obtain a **“Certificate of Residence”** (شهادة سكن) that backs up your claim. | --- ## 3. Parallel move: Get a *school‑registration* document now Even while you are waiting for the Sudanese birth certificate, you can **secure a provisional spot for your son**. Follow these steps: 1. **Gather the following “supporting” documents** (all should be originals or notarised copies): - Your **temporary residence paper** (Sixth of October office) - Your **UNHCR card** or any refugee ID you have - A **passport‑style photo** of your son (3 × 4 cm) - A **letter from the Sudanese Embassy** (even if it only says “we are processing the request”) - Any **medical record** that mentions the child’s name and date of birth (e.g., vaccination card, clinic receipt) 2. **Visit the school’s administration office** and ask for the **“Form for Children without Birth Certificates”** (استمارة الأطفال دون شهادة ميلاد). - In most governorates (Cairo, Giza, Al‑Mansoura, etc.) the form is standard and the principal can sign it. - Fill it out, attach the documents above, and request a **“Certificate of No Objection”** (شهادة عدم ممانعة) from the school. 3. **If the school says “no, you need the birth certificate”**, ask to speak to the **Vice‑Principal or the School’s Legal Advisor** and show them the UNHCR/NGO letters. - Mention **Article 10 of the 2009 Education Law** that guarantees education for all children residing in Egypt. 4. **If the school still refuses**, request a **written refusal** (خطاب رفض) and take it to the **Local Education Directorate (مكتب التربية)** in your district. - Bring all the documents you already have. The directorate can issue a **“Special Enrollment Permit”** (تصريح تسجيل خاص) that forces the school to accept the child. > **Tip:** Keep a **photocopy** of every receipt, email, and letter. If the process drags on, you’ll need a paper trail to prove you’ve been proactive. --- ## 4. Escalation route – When every office sends you in circles | Step | Who to contact | What to say / request | How to document | |------|----------------|-----------------------|-----------------| | **1️⃣ File a complaint with the Ministry of Interior’s “Foreigners’ Affairs” (مكتب شؤون الأجانب)** | Call **+202 2390 3322** or visit the **Foreigners’ Affairs office** in Nasr City (2nd floor, Ministry of Interior building). | “I have been referred from Office A to Office B and back again. I need a clear, written decision on my son’s documentation so he can attend school.” | Write down the name and badge number of the officer you speak to; ask for a **receipt** (إيصال) of the complaint. | | **2️⃣ Contact the Egyptian Ombudsman (ديوان شكاوى المواطن)** | Phone **+202 2390 7070** (toll‑free) or email **ombudsman@ombudsman.gov.eg**. | Submit a **formal complaint** with copies of all letters from the Sudanese Embassy, UNHCR, and the school. State that the administrative loop violates the child’s right to education. | Keep the **case number** the Ombudsman gives you. | | **3️⃣ Seek legal aid from a pro‑bono lawyer** | Call the **Legal Aid Centre (مركز المساعدة القانونية)** at **+202 2468 4444** or email **legalaid@cairo.gov.eg**. | “I need a lawyer to file an administrative petition (دعوى إدارية) against the Education Directorate for refusing to register my child without a birth certificate.” | The lawyer will draft a petition to the **Administrative Court** (محكمة الإدارة) requesting a **“temporary injunction”** that forces the school to enrol the child while the certificate is being processed. | | **4️⃣ If time runs out (e.g., school registration deadline)** | **Contact the local MP (عضو مجلس النواب)** for your district. | “My child cannot start school because of bureaucratic delays. I need your intervention to accelerate the process.” | MPs often have direct lines to the Ministry of Education and can push for a quick resolution. | --- ## 5. Practical tips for navigating the bureaucracy | Tip | Why it helps | |-----|--------------| | **Write everything in Arabic** (even if you speak English). Most officials will not read an English letter. Use simple, clear language. | | **Number every page** and attach a **table of contents** (جدول المحتويات). It makes the file look organised and reduces the chance it gets “lost”. | | **Use a red‑ink “stamp”** on any letter you receive (a small seal you can buy at a stationery shop). It shows you have an official copy. | | **Take a friend or a community leader** with you to any office. A second adult can act as a witness and help you remember what was said. | | **Ask for the officer’s full name, title, and contact number** before you leave. Write it down immediately. | | **Never pay cash without a receipt**. If an office asks for a fee, ask for an official invoice (فاتورة) first. | | **Keep a small “documentation folder”** (plastic file) with:
• All original IDs (passport, UNHCR card, residence paper)
• Copies of every letter you send/receive
• Receipts, stamps, and dates
• A notebook with a timeline of every visit (date, office, officer, outcome). | --- ## 6. Sample letters you can copy‑paste ### A. Email to the Sudanese Embassy (Arabic) ```text الموضوع: طلب استخراج شهادة ميلاد لولدي (عاجل – تسجيل المدرسة) إلى سعادة القنصلية السودانية في القاهرة تحية طيبة وبعد، أنا الموقع أدناه: __________________________ (الاسم الكامل) رقم الإقامة المؤقتة: ______________________ رقم جواز السفر / بطاقة الهوية: ___________ أقيم في القاهرة منذ ___ شهر/سنة. لدي طفل اسمه __________________________ تاريخ الميلاد: __/__/____ مكان الميلاد: الخرطوم، السودان (المنطقة/المستشفى). أحتاج شهادة ميلاد الطفل لتسجيله في مدرسة مصرية، وقد تم إبلاغي بأنه لا يمكنه الالتحاق بالمدرسة بدون هذه الوثيقة. نظراً لعدم قدرتي على السفر إلى السودان في الوقت الحالي، أطلب من سيادتكم التكرم بإصدار شهادة الميلاد وإرسالها إليّ عبر البريد الإلكتروني أو الفاكس، مع إرفاق جميع المستندات المطلوبة. أرفق طيه نسخاً من: 1. بطاقة الإقامة المؤقتة (ورقة مكتب السادس من أكتوبر) 2. نسخة من جواز السفر 3. صورة من شهادة الميلاد الأولية (إن وجدت) 4. أي نموذج طلب تحتاجونه (أرجو إرساله إذا لزم الأمر) أشكر سيادتكم سلفاً على تعاونكم السريع، وأتطلع لاستلام الشهادة في أقرب وقت ممكن. مع خالص التحية، [اسمك الكامل] رقم الهاتف: ___________ البريد الإلكتروني: ___________ ``` ### B. Letter to the school principal (Arabic) ```text السيد/السيدة مدير/ة مدرسة __________ العنوان: _______________________ التاريخ: ___/___/_____ الموضوع: طلب تسجيل طفل دون شهادة ميلاد تحية طيبة، أنا المواطن/ة _________________________ (اسمك الكامل) أحمل إقامة مؤقتة في مصر رقم __________. أود تسجيل طفلي _________________________ (اسم الطفل) في الصف __________ للعام الدراسي ____/____. حسب القانون المصري (المادة 10 من قانون التعليم 2009) يحق لكل طفل مقيم في مصر الالتحاق بالمدرسة بغض النظر عن الوثائق الرسمية. نظراً لكون شهادة ميلاد طفلي صادرة من السودان ولا يمكنني استلامها في الوقت الحالي، أرفق مع هذه الرسالة: 1. نسخة من إقامتي المؤقتة. 2. نسخة من بطاقة هوية/جواز السفر. 3. نسخة من شهادة الهوية الصادرة عن UNHCR (إن وجدت). 4. رسالة من سفارة السودان تفيد بأن طلب استخراج شهادة الميلاد قيد المعالجة. 5. شهادة التطعيم/الطبية التي توضح تاريخ الميلاد. أرجو منكم التكرم بمنحي “شهادة عدم ممانعة” (Certificate of No Objection) أو أي وثيقة مؤقتة تسمح بتسجيل طفلي في المدرسة حتى صدور شهادة الميلاد الرسمية. شاكرًا لكم تعاونكم السريع. مع خالص التحية، [اسمك الكامل] رقم الهاتف: ___________ البريد الإلكتروني: ___________ ``` ### C. Complaint to the Egyptian Ombudsman (English – can be translated) ```text Date: ___/___/____ To: The Office of the Egyptian Ombudsman Address: 1 Kasr El‑Nile St., Cairo, Egypt Subject: Formal complaint – Administrative dead‑end in obtaining my son’s birth certificate for school registration Dear Sir/Madam, I am a resident of Cairo (temporary residence permit issued by the Sixth of October office, attached). My son, [Full Name], was born in Khartoum, Sudan, on [date]. The school where we wish to enroll him requires his Sudanese birth certificate. I have taken the following steps: 1. Requested the birth certificate from the Sudanese Embassy in Cairo (see attached correspondence). The embassy confirmed the request but has not yet issued the document. 2. Contacted UNHCR and NGOs (Caritas Egypt, Jesuit Refugee Service) for a substitute identity document (copies attached). 3. Submitted the school’s “Form for Children without Birth Certificates” together with all supporting documents (see attached). 4. The school referred me to the Local Education Directorate, which in turn sent me back to the school, creating a circular referral loop with no resolution. Despite my repeated attempts, I have been unable to secure a definitive decision, and the school registration deadline is approaching. This situation violates my son’s right to education under Egyptian law (Art. 10 of the 2009 Education Law). I request the Ombudsman’s intervention to: - Obtain a written directive from the Ministry of Education authorising the school to enrol my son without the birth certificate pending its issuance. - Facilitate the issuance of a temporary school‑registration certificate (Certificate of No Objection) from the relevant authorities. I enclose copies of all relevant documents and a log of dates, offices, and officials
